newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Strike paralyzes Venezuelan justice system.
newsitem.headline: Strike paralyzes Venezuelan justice system.

text.p: Judges and legal clerks on strike over pay issues paralysed Venezuela's justice system on Monday even as President Rafael Caldera summoned legislators to consider judicial reforms.
The country's 1,300 judges and 15,000 support staff were protesting in an open-ended strike over a delayed salary bonus totalling $10 million.
Caldera was consulting with Congress and Supreme Court President Cecilia Sosa over plans to reform a justice system that critics say is grossly inept and riddled with corruption.
"Reforms so far have been timid and not gone to the bottom of the problem," said Congressman Orlando Contreras, president of Congress's judicial reform committee.

Judicial reform has become a closely watched issue in Venezuela. Oppostion lawmakers, frustrated with courts that can take up to five years to try a minor robbery, last week floated a plan that would fire all of the country's judges.
Government officials say Caldera, 80, who has made the fight against corruption a personal goal, may create a Judicial Commission to study and implement possible changes.
